B12C301.summary: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to set out the Sankhya philosophy. Bhishma presents its view of the world, the elements and qualities that make up the body and cosmos, the faults of the body, and the path by which the wise rise through the qualities to liberation. Yudhishthira then asks whether a liberated person keeps consciousness, a question he says bears on which way of life is superior.

scenes.B12C301S01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to explain the Sankhya principles, and Bhishma describes the doctrine's view of the world, the body's faults and the way of liberation. Yudhishthira then raises the question of whether consciousness survives liberation.
scenes.B12C301S02: Bhishma answers that the senses serve the soul, that a freed soul merges into Brahma, and that Sankhya knowledge is the source of other learning. He ends by describing Narayana as the one who creates and withdraws the universe.

shots.B12C301S01H01: Yudhishthira praises the account of Yoga he has heard and asks Bhishma to now explain the Sankhya principles.
shots.B12C301S01H02: Bhishma calls the Sankhya doctrine faultless and lists the wise who hold it, then describes their knowledge of the world's faults, the three qualities and the chain of elements leading up to Narayana.
shots.B12C301S01H03: Yudhishthira asks what faults Bhishma sees in the body and asks for a full and true answer.
shots.B12C301S01H04: Bhishma names five bodily faults, explains how each is overcome, and describes the ocean of life that the wise cross to reach the Supreme Soul.
shots.B12C301S01H05: Yudhishthira asks whether the liberated keep memory and consciousness, noting that the answer bears on the two ways of life and on what deep sleep is.
shots.B12C301S02H01: Bhishma calls the question proper but hard, explains that the senses serve the soul and rest in sleep, and says a freed soul merges into Brahma and does not return.
shots.B12C301S02H02: Bhishma says Sankhya knowledge feeds all other learning, that its adherents rise to godly status or to Brahma, and that the wise man who masters it becomes like Narayana, who creates and reabsorbs the universe in cycles.

B12C302.summary: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to explain the difference between the Deteriorating and the Undeteriorating, and Bhishma answers with an old teaching of Vasishtha to king Karala of Janaka's race. Vasishtha describes the cycles of creation and destruction, the sequence of elements and senses that make up every embodied being, and a twenty-fifth principle that lies beyond them. He explains that union with Prakriti makes the Indestructible seem destructible, and that knowledge reveals its true nature.

scenes.B12C302S01: Vasishtha teaches king Karala about the Destructible and the Indestructible, covering the cosmic cycles, the twenty-four principles and the twenty-fifth beyond them.

shots.B12C302S01H01: Yudhishthira asks what the Undeteriorating and the Deteriorating are, and says he wants to hear it all from Bhishma while Bhishma still has time to teach.
shots.B12C302S01H02: Bhishma tells the old story of Vasishtha and king Karala, who asks Vasishtha about the supreme Brahma and what the universe returns to at its destruction.
shots.B12C302S01H03: Vasishtha describes the measure of the cosmic days, the creation of Hiranyagarbha, and the elements and senses that make up every living body, all of which he calls destructible.
shots.B12C302S01H04: Vasishtha names Vishnu as the twenty-fifth principle beyond the twenty-four, and explains how the soul, joined to Prakriti, takes on the three qualities and so falls into different destinies.

B12C303.summary: Vasishtha continues by explaining how the soul, forgetting its true nature, falls under ignorance and is reborn again and again among gods, men and lower beings. He lists the many bodily ailments, ascetic practices, rites and worldly roles the soul takes on while it believes itself bound by them. He says Prakriti drives the cycle of birth, death and acts, and that the soul, though free of all attributes, imagines it has them.

scenes.B12C303S01: Vasishtha describes the endless births and sufferings of the forgetful soul, the bodies and practices it takes on, and the cycle of acts driven by Prakriti.

shots.B12C303S01H01: Vasishtha describes the forgetful soul's endless births and sufferings, the many ascetic and worldly roles it takes on, and the cycle of acts driven by Prakriti.

B12C304.summary: Vasishtha closes the teaching by comparing the soul to the moon, which waxes and wanes while one of its sixteen portions stays constant. Under ignorance the soul is repeatedly reborn, and its pure nature becomes tied to the three qualities of Prakriti. Emancipation is described as release from that union.

scenes.B12C304S01: Vasishtha compares the soul to the moon's sixteen portions, explains how ignorance keeps Jiva in repeated births, and defines emancipation as freedom from Prakriti.

shots.B12C304S01H01: Vasishtha compares Jiva to the moon's sixteen portions, fifteen subject to change and one pure, and says emancipation means release from union with Prakriti.

B12C305.summary: King Janaka asks Vasishtha how Emancipation can exist if Purusha and Prakriti are always joined, as male and female are in creation, and he asks for direct evidence of it. Vasishtha answers that memorized texts without understanding are of no use. He explains that Sankhya and Yoga teach the same truth, that the Supreme Soul is beyond all attributes, and that unity marks the Indestructible while multiplicity marks the destructible.

scenes.B12C305S01: Janaka asks how Emancipation can exist given the constant union of Purusha and Prakriti, and Vasishtha answers that texts must be understood, then explains the Supreme Soul and the difference between unity and multiplicity.

shots.B12C305S01H01: Janaka compares the union of male and female to that of Purusha and Prakriti, asks how Emancipation can then exist, and asks for direct evidence of it.
shots.B12C305S01H02: Vasishtha says memorized texts without understanding are of no use, then argues that Sankhya and Yoga teach the same truth, that the Supreme Soul is beyond attributes, and that unity and multiplicity mark the two kinds of being.

B12C306.summary: Janaka says he is still confused about unity and multiplicity, and asks Vasishtha to explain again the knower, Jiva, knowledge, ignorance, and both the Sankhya and Yoga systems. Vasishtha describes the Yoga practice of contemplation, breath control and stillness, and the vision of the Supreme Soul it brings. He then sets out the Sankhya chain of principles, how they dissolve back in reverse order, and how the Soul is the true knower freed from returning to the world.

scenes.B12C306S01: Janaka asks for a fuller account of unity and multiplicity; Vasishtha explains the Yoga practice of contemplation, then the Sankhya principles and how the Soul is known as the true knower.

shots.B12C306S01H01: Janaka admits he has not grasped unity and multiplicity and asks Vasishtha to explain again the knower, Jiva, knowledge, ignorance, and the Sankhya and Yoga systems in detail.
shots.B12C306S01H02: Vasishtha describes Yoga as contemplation through concentration and breath control, the stillness it demands, and the Supreme Soul that the Yogin sees shining in the heart.
shots.B12C306S01H03: Vasishtha sets out the Sankhya principles from Prakriti down to the senses, their dissolution in reverse order, and the distinction between Kshetra, Kshetrajna and Purusha, and says that one who knows the Soul does not return to the world.

B12C307.summary: Vasishtha defines knowledge (Vidya) and ignorance (Avidya) in terms of the Sankhya principles, with Prakriti as ignorance and the Purusha beyond the twenty-four as knowledge. He explains why both Prakriti and the Jiva can be called indestructible or destructible. He then gives the Jiva's lament at being caught in Prakriti like a fish in a net, and its resolve to turn to the Supreme Soul, before noting that Sankhya and Yoga teach the same knowledge.

scenes.B12C307S01: Vasishtha defines knowledge and ignorance through the Sankhya principles, gives the Jiva's lament at its bondage to Prakriti and its resolve to turn to the Supreme Soul, and notes that Sankhya and Yoga agree.

shots.B12C307S01H01: Vasishtha defines knowledge and ignorance through the principles, explains why both Prakriti and the Jiva are called indestructible and destructible, and gives the Jiva's lament at its bondage to Prakriti.
shots.B12C307S01H02: Vasishtha says Sankhya and Yoga teach the same knowledge, that it can awaken any listener, and that Yoga speaks of Brahma and the Jiva as two only because of ignorance.

B12C308.summary: Vasishtha contrasts the Supreme Soul with the Jiva, which takes on the qualities of Prakriti through ignorance and is freed only by recognizing itself as distinct from her. He says the teaching must be given only to worthy and humble disciples, never to deceitful or unworthy ones. Bhishma closes the whole discourse by tracing its line of transmission from Hiranyagarbha through Vasishtha and Narada to himself, and by assuring the king that knowledge frees him from ignorance.

scenes.B12C308S01: Vasishtha contrasts the Supreme Soul with the Jiva, explains how the Jiva is freed, and says who may receive the teaching. Bhishma then closes the discourse with its line of transmission and an assurance to the king.

shots.B12C308S01H01: Vasishtha contrasts the Supreme Soul with the Jiva, explains how the Jiva is freed by recognizing itself as distinct from Prakriti, and says that a soul takes on the qualities of whatever it unites with.
shots.B12C308S01H02: Vasishtha lists the kinds of people who may and may not receive this knowledge, calls on Karala to be fearless, and says he received the teaching from Hiranyagarbha.
shots.B12C308S01H03: Bhishma closes by tracing the teaching from Hiranyagarbha through Vasishtha and Narada to himself, and tells the king that knowledge of Kshara and Akshara frees him from ignorance.

B12C309.summary: A king of Janaka's race, Vasuman, meets a Rishi of Bhrigu's line while hunting and asks what brings lasting benefit to a man whose body is unstable and whose desires are strong. The Rishi advises restraint, righteous conduct, generous gifts from honestly earned wealth, firmness, and the company of virtuous people. The king accepts the counsel and turns his mind to righteousness.

scenes.B12C309S01: King Vasuman asks a Bhrigu-line Rishi how to gain lasting good, and the Rishi advises righteousness, gifts, firmness and the company of the virtuous. The king takes this advice to heart.

shots.B12C309S01H01: King Vasuman, of Janaka's race, meets a Rishi of Bhrigu's line in the forest and asks what benefits a man with an unstable body and strong desires.
shots.B12C309S01H02: The Rishi advises restraint, righteous conduct, honest gifts, purity, patience and firmness, and keeping company with the virtuous.
shots.B12C309S01H03: Vasuman accepts the counsel and sets his mind on righteousness.
shots.B12C309S01H04: A section heading marking the start of Section CCCXI.

B12C310.summary: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma for teaching on what is free from duty, doubt, birth and death. Bhishma offers an old dialogue in which king Daivarati of Janaka's race questions the Rishi Yajnavalkya about the senses, Prakriti, Brahma and the limits of life. Yajnavalkya begins his answer with the list of principles and the stages of creation.

scenes.B12C310S01: Yudhishthira asks for teaching on the eternal and indestructible, and Bhishma introduces a dialogue in which Janaka questions Yajnavalkya, who begins by listing the principles and the stages of creation.

shots.B12C310S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to teach him about what is beyond duty, doubt, birth and death, and is eternal and free from effort.
shots.B12C310S01H02: Bhishma introduces an old dialogue between Yajnavalkya and king Daivarati of Janaka's race, who asks the Rishi a question.
shots.B12C310S01H03: The king asks how many kinds of senses and Prakriti there are, what the Unmanifest and highest Brahma are, and what birth, death and the limits of age mean.
shots.B12C310S01H04: Yajnavalkya names the eight Prakriti principles and sixteen modifications, then gives the stages of creation that make up the twenty-four principles.

B12C311.summary: Yajnavalkya measures the length of Brahma's day and night and describes how Brahman, born from a golden egg, creates the earth and sky. He then traces the creation of the five elements, their qualities, and the senses. He ends by saying the mind rules the senses, so the senses act only through it.

scenes.B12C311S01: Yajnavalkya describes Brahma's day and night, his emergence from a golden egg, the creation of the elements and senses, and the mind's rule over them.

shots.B12C311S01H01: Yajnavalkya gives the length of Brahma's day and night, describes his emergence from a golden egg, the creation of the elements and the qualities of sound and touch, and says the mind directs the senses.

B12C312.summary: Yajnavalkya explains how creation is dissolved at the end of Brahman's day. Maharudra, urged by the Unmanifest, burns all living things, and then fire, water, wind, space, mind, consciousness and Mahat are each absorbed in turn into Sambhu. He then announces that he will turn to the three frames of teaching, Adhyatma, Adhibhuta and Adhidaivata.

scenes.B12C312S01: Yajnavalkya describes the dissolution of creation at the end of Brahma's day, from Maharudra's fire to the absorption of all into Sambhu, and introduces the three frames of teaching.

shots.B12C312S01H01: Yajnavalkya describes the dissolution of creation, from Maharudra's fire through the absorption of each element into Sambhu, and then announces the three frames of teaching.

B12C313.summary: Yajnavalkya pairs each sense and faculty with three aspects: its inner organ (Adhyatma), its outer object (Adhibhuta), and its presiding deity (Adhidaivata). He then explains that Prakriti multiplies the three qualities into countless forms, and he lists the qualities that belong to Sattwa, Rajas and Tamas. The passage sets up the teaching on the qualities that follows.

scenes.B12C313S01: Yajnavalkya pairs each sense and faculty with its inner, outer and divine aspects, explains how Prakriti multiplies the three qualities, and lists the qualities that belong to each.

shots.B12C313S01H01: Yajnavalkya pairs each sense and faculty with its inner organ, outer object and presiding deity, then describes how Prakriti multiplies the three qualities and lists the traits of Sattwa, Rajas and Tamas.

B12C314.summary: Yajnavalkya explains that the three qualities are present in all things and that their mixtures decide a being's destiny, from the realms of the gods down to the lowest forms of life. He says Purusha stays unchanged, and that Prakriti, though inanimate, creates only when Purusha presides over her. Janaka then asks how one can be called inanimate while the other is intelligent, and asks for teachings on Emancipation, Sankhya, Yoga and the signs of death.

scenes.B12C314S01: Yajnavalkya explains how the three qualities mix to decide rebirth, and how Prakriti creates only under the presence of Purusha. Janaka then asks how the two differ and asks for fuller teaching on Emancipation.

shots.B12C314S01H01: Yajnavalkya explains how the three qualities mix to decide where a being is reborn, and that Prakriti acts only when presided over by Purusha, who remains unchanged.
shots.B12C314S01H02: Janaka asks how Prakriti can be inanimate while Purusha is intelligent, and asks for teaching on Emancipation, Sankhya, Yoga, and the signs of approaching death.

B12C315.summary: Yajnavalkya explains that Purusha seems to take on attributes as a clear crystal takes on the colour of a nearby flower, while in truth he is beyond them. Prakriti, unintelligent by nature, seems alive only through her union with Purusha. He argues that Purusha and Prakriti are distinct, using images such as the worm in the fig, the fish in water and the fire in a pot, and he then turns to the teaching of Yoga.

scenes.B12C315S01: Yajnavalkya explains how Purusha seems bound to attributes while in truth being distinct from Prakriti, illustrates this with several images, and then announces the teaching of Yoga.

shots.B12C315S01H01: Yajnavalkya explains that Purusha seems to take on attributes but is in truth beyond them, that Prakriti seems alive only through union with him, and that the two are distinct, as shown by images like the worm in the fig and the fish in water.

B12C316.summary: Yajnavalkya says Sankhya and Yoga aim at the same liberation and that people who see them as different lack understanding. He describes the Yoga practices of breath and sense control, the eight powers they bring, and the two kinds of practice, with and without attributes. He ends with the stillness of one who is absorbed in Samadhi and beholds the Supreme Soul.

scenes.B12C316S01: Yajnavalkya presents Yoga as one with Sankhya, describes breath and sense control, the eight powers and the two kinds of practice, and portrays the calm of one absorbed in Samadhi.

shots.B12C316S01H01: Yajnavalkya presents Yoga as one with Sankhya, describes breath and sense control, the eight powers and the two kinds of practice, and portrays the calm of one absorbed in Samadhi who beholds the Supreme Soul.

B12C317.summary: Yajnavalkya explains that the exit point of the soul at death decides which heavenly region it reaches, with each part of the body linked to a particular deity or realm. He then lists the bodily and sensory signs that foretell death within a year, six months, a week or a single day. He advises the wise to unite with the Supreme Soul and live in abstinence, so as to overcome death.

scenes.B12C317S01: Yajnavalkya describes where the soul goes depending on the exit point from the body, then lists the signs that foretell death and advises the wise to unite with the Supreme Soul.

shots.B12C317S01H01: Yajnavalkya links each exit point of the soul at death to a heavenly region, then lists the signs that foretell death within a year, six months, a week or a day, and advises the wise to unite with the Supreme Soul.

B12C318.summary: Yajnavalkya recounts how the sun god Surya gave him the Yajush texts, how the goddess Saraswati entered him, and how he compiled the Satapatha Brahmana and taught it to his disciples. He then answers the Gandharva Viswavasu's long list of questions about the universe, Prakriti, Purusha, knowledge and ignorance, and the Supreme Soul. He ends by saying that liberation comes through knowledge that is open to every order of people, and Bhishma adds how king Daivarati gave up his kingdom to live as a renunciant.

scenes.B12C318S01: Yajnavalkya recounts receiving the Yajush texts and compiling the Satapatha Brahmana, then answers the Gandharva Viswavasu's questions on Prakriti, Purusha and the Supreme Soul.
scenes.B12C318S02: Yajnavalkya says liberation comes through knowledge open to all orders, and Bhishma describes how king Daivarati handed his kingdom to his son and took up the life of a renunciant.

shots.B12C318S01H01: Yajnavalkya tells how Surya granted him the Yajush texts, how Saraswati entered him, and how he received the Satapatha Brahmana and taught it to his disciples.
shots.B12C318S01H02: Yajnavalkya says he taught fifty branches of learning, then recounts the Gandharva Viswavasu's long list of questions on the universe, Vedic lore and Vidya.
shots.B12C318S01H03: Viswavasu asks Yajnavalkya to discourse again on the Jiva and the Supreme Soul, naming many earlier teachers whose views he has heard.
shots.B12C318S01H04: Yajnavalkya explains that Prakriti is known by Jiva, that Purusha is unchanging and distinct from Prakriti, and that Vedic study without this knowledge is a useless burden.
shots.B12C318S01H05: Viswavasu praises Yajnavalkya's answers and blesses him.
shots.B12C318S02H01: Viswavasu departs and spreads the teaching, and Yajnavalkya says liberation comes from knowledge, which is open to every order of people.
shots.B12C318S02H02: Bhishma describes king Daivarati's gifts, his handing of the kingdom to his son, his life as a renunciant, and his teaching that the Supreme must be known and the Soul is its own possession.

B12C319.summary: Yudhishthira asks whether great power, wealth and long life can be kept safe from death and decay by penance, ritual, knowledge or medicine. Bhishma offers the old dialogue in which Janaka of the Videhas asks the sage Panchasikha the same question. Panchasikha answers that time carries every creature along without a raft, and that only the eternal path of renunciation leads beyond birth and death.

scenes.B12C319S01: Yudhishthira asks how death can be avoided, and Bhishma tells the old dialogue in which Janaka questions the sage Panchasikha, who says that only renunciation leads beyond birth and death.

shots.B12C319S01H01: Yudhishthira asks whether penance, ritual, knowledge of the Srutis or medicine can prevent decrepitude and death, after great power and wealth.
shots.B12C319S01H02: Bhishma tells of Janaka's question to the sage Panchasikha, who answers that time sweeps all creatures on, and that only the path of renunciation escapes birth and death.

B12C320.summary: Yudhishthira asks whether liberation can be won while living a householder's life. Bhishma tells how the mendicant Sulabha, having heard that king Dharmadhyaja of Janaka's line was devoted to renunciation, enters his mind by Yoga power to test him. The king claims his freedom is compatible with ruling and rebukes her, and Sulabha answers at length, defending her conduct and arguing that souls cannot be mixed by contact. Janaka, hearing her reasoning, has no reply.

scenes.B12C320S01: Bhishma tells how the mendicant Sulabha tests king Janaka's freedom by entering his mind through Yoga, and the two debate at length on renunciation, kingship and the purity of the soul.
scenes.B12C320S02: Bhishma notes that Janaka, having heard Sulabha's reasoning, has no answer.

shots.B12C320S01H01: Yudhishthira asks how one can gain Emancipation without leaving the householder's life, and how the gross and subtle bodies are cast off.
shots.B12C320S01H02: Bhishma tells of king Dharmadhyaja, devoted to renunciation, whose fame leads the mendicant Sulabha to take a beautiful form by Yoga, visit his court and bind his mind to hers.
shots.B12C320S01H03: Janaka asks who Sulabha is, says he is a disciple of Panchasikha, argues that kingship does not bar freedom, and rebukes her conduct and her motive.
shots.B12C320S01H04: Bhishma says Sulabha is not abashed by the rebuke.
shots.B12C320S01H05: Sulabha replies with a long argument on the rules of debate, the limits of kingship, the separateness of souls, and her own birth and purpose in coming to the king.
shots.B12C320S02H01: Bhishma says that Janaka, hearing these words, could not reply.

B12C321.summary: Yudhishthira asks how Suka, son of Vyasa, came to renounce the world. Vyasa, seeing his son living carelessly, gives him a long exhortation to master the senses, practise truth and righteousness, honour the wise and prepare for death, which takes each person alone with only his deeds. Moved by these words, Suka leaves home to seek a teacher of the path to liberation.

scenes.B12C321S01: Vyasa urges his son Suka at length to master the senses, live righteously and prepare for death, and Suka then leaves to seek a teacher of liberation.

shots.B12C321S01H01: Yudhishthira asks how Suka, son of Vyasa, was won over to renunciation, and asks for teaching on the Unmanifest, the Manifest and Brahma.
shots.B12C321S01H02: Vyasa, seeing his son careless, urges him to master the senses, practise truth and righteousness, honour the wise, and prepare for death, which will take him alone with only his deeds.
shots.B12C321S01H03: Suka, moved by his father's words, leaves to seek a teacher who can teach the path to liberation.

B12C322.summary: Yudhishthira asks whether gifts, sacrifices, penance and service to teachers really bring benefit. Bhishma answers that evil conduct brings poverty and fear, while faith, restraint and generosity bring joy and heaven. Every deed, good or bad, ripens at its proper time and follows the doer, even into the next life.

scenes.B12C322S01: Bhishma explains that sinful acts bring hardship and righteous acts bring joy, since every deed ripens in its own time and follows the doer into the next life.

shots.B12C322S01H01: Yudhishthira asks whether gifts, sacrifices, penances and service to elders have real efficacy, and asks Bhishma to speak of it.
shots.B12C322S01H02: Bhishma says evil conduct brings poverty and fear, while faith, self-restraint and generosity bring joy, and that every deed follows its doer and ripens at its proper time.

B12C323.summary: Yudhishthira asks how Suka, the son of Vyasa, was born and why his mind turned to the subtle Brahma so early. Bhishma says that merit rests on restraining the senses, and tells how Vyasa, after long penance on Mount Meru, won from Mahadeva the boon of a son of great purity.

scenes.B12C323S01: Bhishma explains that Suka's greatness comes from restraint, and recounts how Vyasa's long penance before Mahadeva on Mount Meru won him the promise of a son.

shots.B12C323S01H01: Yudhishthira asks how Suka was born, how he came to be drawn to Brahma as a boy, and how he reached his goal.
shots.B12C323S01H02: Bhishma says merit lies in restraining the senses, and tells how Vyasa, meditating on Mahadeva on Mount Meru, asks for a son and is granted one.

B12C324.summary: Vyasa's desire for the apsara Ghritachi causes his seed to fall while he is kindling a fire, and Suka is born from the fire-sticks. The gods and celestial beings celebrate, Mahadeva invests the boy with the sacred thread, and Suka masters the Vedas under the teacher Vrihaspati. Even as a youth his mind is set on the path of liberation rather than household life.

scenes.B12C324S01: Vyasa's desire for Ghritachi leads to Suka's birth from the fire-sticks, the gods celebrate, and Suka studies the Vedas under Vrihaspati and turns toward liberation.

shots.B12C324S01H01: Bhishma tells how Vyasa's desire for the apsara Ghritachi leads to Suka's birth from the fire-sticks, how the gods celebrate, and how Suka masters the Vedas under Vrihaspati before turning toward liberation.

B12C325.summary: Vyasa sends his son Suka to king Janaka of Mithila to learn the path to liberation, and tells him to travel on foot like ordinary people and to show humility. Suka makes his way across many lands and is kept waiting at the palace gate. He is then tested by a troupe of palace women, but remains unmoved and spends the night in Yoga.

scenes.B12C325S01: Vyasa sends Suka to Janaka, Suka walks to Mithila, is kept waiting and tested by palace women, and remains calm, spending the night absorbed in Yoga.

shots.B12C325S01H01: Vyasa sends Suka to king Janaka, Suka walks to Mithila, is tested by palace women, and spends the night absorbed in Yoga.

B12C326.summary: King Janaka receives Suka with full honour and asks the purpose of his visit. Suka asks what a Brahmana's duties are and whether a man of purified understanding must still pass through the four stages of life. Janaka explains that right knowledge, guided by a teacher, is the boat that carries one across the world's ocean, and tells Suka that he already has that knowledge.

scenes.B12C326S01: Janaka receives Suka with honour, and the two discuss the four stages of life. Janaka explains that knowledge is the means to liberation and tells Suka that he already has it.

shots.B12C326S01H01: Janaka receives Suka with honour, offering a costly seat, water, and kine, and asks the purpose of his visit.
shots.B12C326S01H02: Suka says his father sent him to learn the duties of a Brahmana and the path to Emancipation, and asks whether knowledge or penance leads there.
shots.B12C326S01H03: Janaka describes the stages of a Brahmana's life, from study and household life to forest life and renunciation.
shots.B12C326S01H04: Suka asks whether a man with a purified understanding must still pass through the stages of life.
shots.B12C326S01H05: Janaka says understanding and true knowledge are required, that a teacher is the helmsman and knowledge the boat, and that Suka already has the knowledge and has passed beyond the objects of the senses.

B12C327.summary: Satisfied, Suka leaves Mithila for the Himalayas, passing stories of Skanda's dart and Mahadeva's penance, and reaches his father Vyasa, who is teaching disciples there. His disciples then ask Vyasa for a boon that the Vedas be shared only among them, and Vyasa sets out rules on who may receive Vedic teaching and how it should be given.

scenes.B12C327S01: Suka returns to the Himalayas and reports to his father Vyasa, and the disciples then ask a boon that Vyasa answers with rules for teaching the Vedas.

shots.B12C327S01H01: Suka goes north to the Himalayas, passing scenes of Skanda's dart and Mahadeva's penance, and reports his conversation with Janaka to his father Vyasa, who is teaching disciples there.
shots.B12C327S01H02: The disciples ask Vyasa for a boon that no sixth disciple should share the Vedas, and Vyasa sets out rules on who may receive Vedic teaching and how it should be given.

B12C328.summary: Vyasa's disciples leave the mountain to teach and perform sacrifices among the people, and Vyasa is left alone with Suka, troubled by the silence of Vedic recitation. Narada points out that the Vedas are lost when they are not recited, and urges Vyasa to resume with his son. A violent wind interrupts their recitation, and Vyasa explains the winds and the two paths after death before going to bathe in the Ganges.

scenes.B12C328S01: Vyasa's disciples leave to spread the Vedas, Narada reproaches Vyasa for the silence of recitation, and Vyasa answers with a long account of the winds and the two paths after death.

shots.B12C328S01H01: Vyasa's disciples leave to teach and perform sacrifices among people, and Vyasa is left alone with Suka, troubled, until Narada arrives.
shots.B12C328S01H02: Narada says the silence of Vedic recitation has robbed the mountain of its beauty, and Vyasa asks what he should do.
shots.B12C328S01H03: Narada says the stain of the Vedas is the halting of their recitation, and urges Vyasa to recite with his son and drive away the fears caused by Rakshasas.
shots.B12C328S01H04: A violent wind interrupts their recitation, and Vyasa treats it as an omen, then explains the winds and the two paths of the gods and the fathers after death.
shots.B12C328S01H05: When the wind has passed, Vyasa tells Suka to resume reciting and goes off to bathe in the Ganges.

B12C329.summary: Narada visits Suka, who honours him and asks what will help him most. Narada passes on the teaching of Sanatkumara, that attachment brings sorrow and that desire and wrath destroy one's good. He describes the river of life that must be crossed by the boat of the body, and says that even the understanding must be cast off through knowledge of the Supreme Soul.

scenes.B12C329S01: Narada visits Suka and passes on Sanatkumara's teaching on detachment, the crossing of the river of life, and the knowledge of the Supreme Soul.

shots.B12C329S01H01: Narada visits Suka, who honours him and asks what will help him most.
shots.B12C329S01H02: Narada, recalling Sanatkumara, urges Suka to restrain desire and wrath, drop attachment, meet all creatures with friendship, and cross the river of life by the boat of the body, casting off even the understanding through knowledge of the Supreme Soul.

B12C330.summary: Narada counsels Suka that wisdom is the cure for sorrow, since grieving over what is past only doubles one's pain. He says that wealth, youth, life and union all end in loss, so one should cultivate contentment, guard the senses and find peace in the self. The man who turns his mind inward and needs nothing from outside reaches happiness.

scenes.B12C330S01: Narada advises Suka that wisdom, not grief, is the cure for sorrow, and that contentment and self-control bring happiness, since all worldly things are transitory.

shots.B12C330S01H01: Narada advises that wisdom lets a person avoid grieving over the past, that grief doubles sorrow, and that contentment, guarding the senses and finding peace in the self bring happiness.

B12C331.summary: Narada explains that fortune, misfortune, the results of childbirth and disease, and the soul's passage from one body to the next are all beyond human control, and that only the self can be protected. Suka reflects on this teaching and resolves to reach an eternal and fearless state through Yoga, even by entering the sun. He takes leave of his father, who asks him to stay, and departs for Kailasa.

scenes.B12C331S01: Narada describes how fortune, suffering and rebirth lie beyond human control, and Suka resolves to attain an eternal state through Yoga, then takes leave of his father and goes to Kailasa.

shots.B12C331S01H01: Narada describes the uncertainty of fortune, the sufferings of birth and disease, and the soul's passage from one body to the next, and says that the deities were once men taught to leave the Earth.
shots.B12C331S01H02: Suka weighs this teaching, decides to reach an eternal state through Yoga, resolves to enter the sun, and departs for Kailasa after taking leave of his father, who asked him to stay.

B12C332.summary: Suka sits in Yoga on a mountain peak, sees his own soul, and rises through the sky, where heavenly beings and Apsaras marvel at him. He tells Narada that he has found the path to liberation, and asks the points of the compass, forests, seas, rivers and mountains to answer his father's calls once he has gone beyond reach. They agree to do so.

scenes.B12C332S01: Suka enters Yoga on a mountain, rises into the sky to the wonder of the heavenly beings, and asks the world to answer his father's calls when he has gone.

shots.B12C332S01H01: Suka sits in Yoga on a mountain peak, sees his own soul freed from attachment, and begins his Yoga practice.
shots.B12C332S01H02: Suka tells Narada that he has seen the path to Emancipation and asks for his blessing.
shots.B12C332S01H03: Suka rises through the sky, passes the Apsaras and Urvasi, and asks the world to answer his father's calls once he is gone, and they agree.

B12C333.summary: Suka sheds all the attributes and dwells in Brahma, and the heavens react with omens as he breaks through the twin peaks of Himavat and Meru. His father Vyasa follows and grieves, calling his name, until Suka answers only as an echo that still sounds in mountains. Mahadeva consoles Vyasa, telling him that his son has reached the highest end and that a shadow of him will remain at Vyasa's side.

scenes.B12C333S01: Suka passes into Brahma with cosmic omens, and Vyasa grieves until Mahadeva consoles him with the promise of his son's fame and a shadow of him.

shots.B12C333S01H01: Bhishma describes Suka's passing into Brahma with cosmic omens, Vyasa's grief at a son who answers only as an echo, and Mahadeva's consolation that the son's fame will last and his shadow will remain with Vyasa.

B12C334.summary: Yudhishthira asks who is the highest deity and the highest Pitri, and how emancipation and lasting heaven can be reached. Bhishma relates how Narada visited Narayana, who had taken fourfold form as the sons of Dharma, and praised him as the source of all. Narayana replies that the inner soul, called Kshetrajna, is the highest object of worship, that unmanifest Prakriti is its companion, and that those who know him are merged into him.

scenes.B12C334S01: Yudhishthira asks about the highest deity and the path to Emancipation, and Bhishma relates Narada's visit to Narayana, who teaches that the inner soul is the highest object of worship.

shots.B12C334S01H01: Yudhishthira asks who is the highest deity and Pitri, what rites should be performed, and how one attains heaven and Emancipation.
shots.B12C334S01H02: Bhishma says the question is a deep mystery and recounts how Narada visited Narayana and Nara at their hermitage, after Narayana took fourfold form as the sons of Dharma.
shots.B12C334S01H03: Narada praises Narayana as unborn, eternal and the source of the universe, and asks whom Narayana worships.
shots.B12C334S01H04: Narayana explains that the inner soul, Kshetrajna, beyond the three qualities is the highest object of worship, that unmanifest Prakriti is its companion, and that the Prajapatis obeyed this law.
shots.B12C334S01H05: A section heading marking the start of Section CCCXXXVI.

B12C335.summary: After Narayana's teaching, Narada visits the White Island, whose strange inhabitants Yudhishthira asks about. Bhishma then tells how King Uparichara, a devotee of Narayana, was tied to the treatise of duties composed by the seven seers under Narayana's command. He explains that this treatise was to be passed down through Vrihaspati, and that it would be lost with the king's death.

scenes.B12C335S01: Narada visits the White Island, Yudhishthira asks about its inhabitants, and Bhishma tells the story of King Uparichara and the treatise composed by the seven seers.

shots.B12C335S01H01: Bhishma says that Narada, after Narayana's teaching, addresses Narayana for the good of the world.
shots.B12C335S01H02: Narada asks Narayana's leave to see his original nature, then goes to the White Island and describes its inhabitants, who have no senses, do not eat, and have winkless eyes.
shots.B12C335S01H03: Yudhishthira asks how the White Island people were born, what end they reach, and whether emancipated men share their marks.
shots.B12C335S01H04: Bhishma tells of King Uparichara, a devotee of Narayana, and how the seven seers, at Narayana's command, compose a treatise on duties that is to be passed down through Vrihaspati.

B12C336.summary: At king Uparichara's great Horse-sacrifice, where no animals are slain and Vrihaspati presides, Hari takes his share unseen, and Vrihaspati is angry. The Sadasyas calm him, and the sons of Brahman describe their penance, their journey to the White Island and the voice that told them only the favour of its devout people brings the sight of Narayana. Vasu later falls through a Brahmana's curse and rises again through Narayana's grace.

scenes.B12C336S01: Vrihaspati presides over Uparichara's sacrifice, Hari takes his share unseen, and the Sadasyas calm Vrihaspati with the account of the White Island and Vasu's fall and rise.

shots.B12C336S01H01: Bhishma tells how Vrihaspati became the priest of king Uparichara's Horse-sacrifice, where no animals were slain, and how Hari took his share unseen, angering Vrihaspati.
shots.B12C336S01H02: Yudhishthira asks why Hari alone took his share invisibly when the other deities appeared openly.
shots.B12C336S01H03: The Sadasyas calm Vrihaspati, and the sons of Brahman describe their penance, their journey to the White Island and the voice that told them that only the favour of its people brings the sight of Narayana, and the chapter ends with Vasu's fall and rise.

B12C337.summary: Yudhishthira asks why king Vasu fell from heaven and was sunk into the earth despite his devotion to Narayana. Bhishma tells how the gods and Rishis argued over whether sacrifices should use animals or grain, and how Vasu, judging for the gods, was cursed to fall. The gods secured him provisions, and Narayana sent Garuda to lift him back to heaven.

scenes.B12C337S01: The gods and Rishis dispute whether sacrifices should use goats or grain, and Vasu is asked to judge between them.
scenes.B12C337S02: Vasu sides with the gods and is cursed to fall, and the gods and Narayana then provide for him and lift him back to heaven. Bhishma then turns to Narada's journey to the White Island.

shots.B12C337S01H01: Yudhishthira asks why king Vasu, so devoted to Narayana, fell from heaven and was sunk into the earth.
shots.B12C337S01H02: Bhishma recounts an old debate in which the gods urge that goats be sacrificed, since the word aja is understood to mean a goat.
shots.B12C337S01H03: The Rishis reply that the Vedas call for seed offerings and that slaughter cannot be the religion of the Krita age.
shots.B12C337S01H04: Vasu comes through the sky, and the gods and Rishis ask him to judge which kind of offering is right.
shots.B12C337S01H05: The Rishis say sacrifices should use grain, while the gods say animals, and both sides ask Vasu to decide.
shots.B12C337S02H01: Vasu sides with the gods and is cursed to fall from heaven; the gods then provide for him, and Narayana sends Garuda to lift him back to the sky.
shots.B12C337S02H02: Bhishma says he has told the origin of the spiritual sons of Brahman and now turns to Narada's journey to the White Island.

B12C338.summary: Narada reaches the White Island, where the white people honour him, and he settles there in silent recitation and Yoga. He then praises Narayana in a long hymn that lists his many forms, as the soul beyond attributes, the source of the Vedas, sacrifices, deities and the cosmos. He closes by saying he is a devoted disciple who longs to see the god.

scenes.B12C338S01: Narada reaches the White Island, takes up silent Yoga there, and offers Narayana a long hymn of praise.

shots.B12C338S01H01: Narada reaches the White Island, is honoured by its people, and begins silent recitation and Yoga there with his arms raised.
shots.B12C338S01H02: Narada's long hymn praises Narayana through a litany of names and forms, as the soul beyond attributes, the source of the Vedas, sacrifices and the gods, and ends with his wish to behold him.

B12C339.summary: Narada's hymn brings Narayana before him in a wondrous universal form, and the god explains his nature as the Purusha beyond the attributes, his fourfold manifestation, and his successive descents into the world. Narada then goes to Vadari and later repeats the teaching in Brahman's abode. Bhishma explains how the narrative has been handed down and that hearing it with devotion brings the highest end, and the frame closes with the recitation at Naimisha.

scenes.B12C339S01: Narada's hymn brings Narayana before him in universal form, and the god explains his nature, his fourfold manifestation and his descents, then sends Narada back to repeat the teaching.
scenes.B12C339S02: Yudhishthira asks why Brahman did not know Narayana's greatness, Bhishma traces how the narrative was handed down and commends it to devotees, and the frame closes with Vaisampayana's words and Suta's account of the sacrifice at Naimisha.

shots.B12C339S01H01: Narayana appears to Narada in a wondrous universal form with a thousand eyes, many heads and arms, and holding the emblems of sacrifice.
shots.B12C339S01H02: Narayana tells Narada that he has been devoted and that the sages Ekata, Dwita and Trita could not see him, then promises him a boon.
shots.B12C339S01H03: Narada says that seeing Narayana is the highest boon, and calls him the Lord whose eye is the universe.
shots.B12C339S01H04: Narayana explains his nature as the Purusha beyond the attributes, the source and dissolution of the universe, his fourfold form, and his descents as boar, man-lion, Rama, Krishna and Kalki.
shots.B12C339S01H05: Narayana vanishes, and Narada goes to Vadari and later repeats the teaching in Brahman's abode.
shots.B12C339S02H01: Yudhishthira asks why Brahman, the Creator, was unaware of Narayana's greatness, which Narada had made known.
shots.B12C339S02H02: Bhishma explains that Brahman honours Narayana as supreme, traces how the narrative passed through Surya, the sages, Asita and Santanu, and says hearing it with devotion leads to the highest end.
shots.B12C339S02H03: Vaisampayana says that Yudhishthira and his brothers became devoted to Narayana, and that Vyasa chanted Narayana's name and returned to his hermitage.
shots.B12C339S02H04: Bhishma closes by saying he has repeated the narrative he heard from his father.
shots.B12C339S02H05: Suta closes the frame, saying that Janamejaya was guided by the recitation and that the listeners at Saunaka's sacrifice in Naimisha should worship Narayana.

B12C340.summary: Saunaka asks why Narayana, who ordains renunciation, also grants the deities shares in sacrifice. Sauti relays Vaisampayana's answer to king Janamejaya, recalling how Vyasa taught his disciples that creation flows from the Supreme Soul through Aniruddha and the eight Prakritis, and how the gods came to Brahman for their roles. Narayana then grants the gods their shares in sacrifice, foretells the decline of righteousness through the four ages, and charges Brahman with the work of creation.

scenes.B12C340S01: Sauti introduces Vaisampayana's answer to Janamejaya, which recalls Vyasa's account of creation through Aniruddha and the eight Prakritis, and the gods' appeal to Brahman.
scenes.B12C340S02: Narayana grants the gods shares in sacrifice and foretells the decline of righteousness through the four ages, and Brahman sees him in a horse-headed form.
scenes.B12C340S03: Narayana charges Brahman with creation and vanishes, and Vaisampayana closes by describing the blessings that come to those who hear and recite the narrative.

shots.B12C340S01H01: Saunaka asks why Narayana, who ordains abstention, also makes the deities takers of shares in sacrifice.
shots.B12C340S01H02: Sauti says he will recite what Vaisampayana told king Janamejaya when the king asked the same question.
shots.B12C340S01H03: Janamejaya asks why the gods, who take shares in sacrifice, have not turned to the path of liberation, and asks for the reason.
shots.B12C340S01H04: Vaisampayana says that Vyasa answered this doubt by describing creation from the Supreme Soul through Aniruddha, the eight Prakritis and the Rudras, and the gods' request to Brahman for their roles.
shots.B12C340S01H05: Brahman tells the gods to seek guidance from the unmanifest Being, and they go to the Ocean of Milk and perform severe penance for a thousand years.
shots.B12C340S02H01: Narayana speaks to the assembled gods, promising to increase their strength and granting them shares in sacrifice.
shots.B12C340S02H02: Vaisampayana says the gods and Brahman hold a sacrifice to Vishnu, who accepts the offerings unseen and promises that human sacrifices will give the gods their shares.
shots.B12C340S02H03: The gods ask where they should go when righteousness declines in the coming ages.
shots.B12C340S02H04: Narayana answers that the gods should seek places where the Vedas, sacrifices, penance and truth still flourish, and that sin will not touch them there.
shots.B12C340S02H05: Vyasa says that Brahman, left alone, sees Narayana appear with a horse's head, and Narayana embraces him.
shots.B12C340S03H01: Narayana charges Brahman with the ordering of creation, promises to appear in incarnate forms when needed, and vanishes, and Brahman returns to his own region.
shots.B12C340S03H02: Vaisampayana closes by saying that whoever hears or recites this discourse with devotion gains health, wealth, sons and fulfilment of desires.

B12C341.summary: King Janamejaya asks Vaisampayana to explain the meanings of the names by which Vyasa and his disciples praised Hari. Vaisampayana recalls how Arjuna once asked Krishna the same thing. Krishna explains that his names arise from his nature and deeds, including Narayana, Vasudeva, Vishnu, Damodara and Kesava, and that he and Rudra are one.

scenes.B12C341S01: Janamejaya asks for the meanings of Hari's names, and Vaisampayana recounts Krishna's explanation to Arjuna of how his names arise from his nature and deeds.

shots.B12C341S01H01: Janamejaya asks Vaisampayana to explain the meanings of the names by which Vyasa and his disciples hymned Hari.
shots.B12C341S01H02: Vaisampayana says that Arjuna once asked Krishna about the meaning of some of his names.
shots.B12C341S01H03: Arjuna asks Krishna to explain the names found in the Vedas and Puranas, since none but Krishna can do so.
shots.B12C341S01H04: Krishna explains that his names come from his nature and deeds, names Narayana, Vasudeva, Vishnu, Damodara and Kesava, and says that he and Rudra are one, and that the best worshippers seek him alone.

B12C342.summary: Arjuna asks how Agni and Soma came to share one nature, and Krishna answers with a long account of creation from the primal darkness, the honour owed to Brahmanas, and many stories of gods who were cursed or saved. These include Indra's sins, Viswarupa's death, Nahusha's fall, Soma's waning and the marks on the moon, and the origins of many of Krishna's own names. Arjuna then asks who won the battle between Rudra and Narayana, and Krishna explains that Brahma stopped it and the two made peace, each marking the other.

scenes.B12C342S01: Krishna narrates the origin of Agni and Soma, the stories of Indra and the Brahmanas, many of his own names, and the battle between Rudra and Narayana that ends in peace.
scenes.B12C342S02: Krishna concludes that Rudra and Narayana are one, and tells Arjuna to bow to Rudra, whom he calls his own wrath-born form.

shots.B12C342S01H01: Arjuna asks how Agni and Soma came to share one original nature.
shots.B12C342S01H02: Krishna recounts the origin of Agni and Soma from Brahman, the honour of Brahmanas, and the stories of Indra's sins, Viswarupa's death, Nahusha's fall and Indra's restoration.
shots.B12C342S01H03: Krishna tells more stories, including Soma's curse and the marks on the moon, and explains many of his own names, such as Hari, Govinda, Krishna and Kapila.
shots.B12C342S01H04: Arjuna asks who won the battle between Rudra and Narayana.
shots.B12C342S01H05: Krishna describes the omens of the battle, Brahma's plea to stop it, and the peace in which Narayana and Rudra mark each other's bodies.
shots.B12C342S02H01: Krishna says that Rudra is his wrath-born form, that the two are one, and that Arjuna should bow to Rudra, who first slew the foes Arjuna has defeated.
